To address the core problem in your section described under "Q1: Data model for merged phases," we essentially need two source parents and two source species, as the new evolutionary path now always has both sources changing. We are only ever merging with an upstream candidate from a source-parent's evolutionary line if that source parent does not have an equivalent phase (such as Rattata only having a Phase 1 evolution, Raticate, and Dratini having a Phase 2 evolution, Dragonite). Your recommended solution to this sounds good to me.

To address the follow-up questions:

1. Ideally, it would show the text similar to what you are describing. Honestly, it would be great to combine the names into one, and show those as the options for evolution, even the name set for the egg/hatched-pokemon. We would simply take the first half of the parent-A's name (rounded up for an odd count of letters) and append on the last half of the parent-B's name (rounded up for an odd count of letters). If the merge has multiple siblings, set the name by averaging the length of all sibling names, chunking the outcome name to the number of sibling evolutions, and iterating through the list of siblings, chunking the name of each sibling, and taking that respective chunk from their name. Prioritize first based on the evolution path chosen, being the leading name prefix, followed by the priority parent from our 62%/50% determination. If there is a tie (like our 50%) determine upfront which parent will be priority (coin-flip when breeding) and keep that recorded in our profile.

2. I'm having a hard time answering this directly, so I am going to try answering this by example. Say we have performed our berserk-gene-editing pokemon fusion breeding thing between Rattata and Applin as a 50% combo. Not all evolutionary line are available, as we select from each parent with a 50% chance. We would always have our Rattata->Raticate evolutionary line as we always need at least one evolution from each parent. However, maybe we only two of the potential evolutionary lines from Applin being Appletun and Dipplin. When an evolutionary line is selected to be available in the resulting Pokemon, the entire line is available. So, we can choose to evolve into Appletun (also merges in the same evolution phase from the other parent if available which is Raticate in this case) or Dipplin (also merges in the same evolution phase from the other parent if available which is Raticate in this case) or Raticate (merges in both Appletun and Dipplin, as the other parent has these as both sibling branches). Chosing to evolve into Dipplin or Raticate provides another optional stage of evolution (Hydrapple when leveled-up while knowing Dragon Cheer) as Dipplin was part of the fusion, while chosing the Appletun path does not provide another stage of evolution as it did not include Dipplin in the fusion.
This full evolutionary line potential needs to be calculated and stored at the time of breeding because, if this Pokemon is born female, it can be re-bred without using the berserk-gene-editing feature, resulting in the exact same berserk-gene-profile on the child (albeit using the standard roll for IVs and abilities and whatever else standard breeding does).
If this fusion child is re-bred using our berserk-gene-editing feature, the same pattern occurs as before. Say we now merge this Pokemon with Eevee using a 62% split. Maybe we select 3 (roughly one-third of 8 rounded up) potential evolutionary lines from Eevee (Sylveon, Umbreon, and Jolteon) as well as 2 (roughly two thirds of 3) from our already-fused parent (Raticate and Dipplin). The resulting Pokemon now has 5 potential evolutionary lines.
If we start reaching our evolutionary line potential (I think I remember us setting it to 8), and one or more of the parents have existing berserk-gene-profiles (have been merged before), prioritize purging the oldest evolutionary lines first.
Say we enter the child from this second wave of berserk-gene-editing-breeding into a third round and merge in Dratini at 50%. Now we have parent-A (Dratini), without an existing berserk-gene-profile, with one evolutionary line and our super-merged parent The-Thing with 5 potential evolutionary lines. We would need to select at least one evolutionary line from each parent, so we could end up with a result that has the potential evolutions of Dragonair, Sylveon, and Dipplin only.
The last fusion here only resulted in 3 potential evolutionary lines. I can't think of a way we would reach our maximum evolutions or exceed it, but if we somehow did, the last merge shows how the Raticate and Dipplin potential evolutions are the oldest of all potential evolutionary routes. These would be the first to be purged. Prioritize the oldest first, then the line with the least evolutionary phases, then randomly on race-conditions.
